context: Add node_modules to the codespell --skip list in the Makefile spellcheck target (and consider results-explorer/dist and any other generated JS output). Prefer making codespell ignore-file aware, or drive the skip list from .gitignore, over hand-maintaining a parallel exclusion list that will drift again. Do NOT weaken --ignore-words. Then re-run the original item's rung with node_modules actually present, which is the check that was never performed. Also worth asking why a done item's rung was not executed - that is a process gap beyond this fix.
description: spellcheck-scans-gitignored-node-modules is marked done, but the fix is not in the tree and that item's own verification rung ('make spellcheck exits 0 with node_modules present') fails. Makefile:942 passes --skip="*.pyc,_build,*.json,*.lock,*.svg,*.min.js,*.min.css,_binaries,*.tpl,*.dst,*.tbl,_sources,benchmark_runs,*.dat,*.pdf,_project,_blog,htmlcov,.venv" - no node_modules and no results-explorer entry, and codespell does not honour .gitignore. Reproduced on develop @ 74aee99: creating results-explorer/node_modules/pkg/index.js containing 'recieve teh occured' makes make spellcheck report three hits and exit non-zero (Error 65). Impact: make pr-preflight is red for every developer who has installed the results-explorer npm deps, which trains people to ignore a real gate. Either the fix was reverted or the item was completed without it landing.

preserves.behavior: Real source-tree typos are still caught; --ignore-words behaviour unchanged

verifications.command: mkdir -p results-explorer/node_modules/pkg && printf 'recieve teh occured\n' > results-explorer/node_modules/pkg/index.js && make spellcheck; rc=$?; rm -rf results-explorer/node_modules; exit $rc
verifications.description: spellcheck passes with gitignored node_modules present
